text.en: Meena saw paddy and wheat on a food table. "Where do these grow?" she asked.

Agriculture supplies food, raw materials and work. Kharif, rabi and zaid are broad seasons, and dates vary by crop and region. Rice is commonly grown as a kharif crop, while wheat is commonly a rabi crop.
Major crops are rice, wheat, millets, pulses, sugarcane, cotton, jute, tea and coffee. Rice grows in the wet plains and deltas, wheat in the Ganga plains, tea in Assam and the Nilgiris and cotton in black soil regions.
Soils include alluvial, black, red, laterite and desert soils. Irrigation by canals, tanks and wells supports farming. The Green Revolution brought high-yielding seeds, and issues like soil erosion need soil conservation.
Agriculture is an important source of food, raw materials and work in India.
Kharif crops generally follow the southwest monsoon. Rabi crops are usually sown after the monsoon and harvested in spring. Zaid is a short season between them.
Rice is a common kharif example, and wheat is a common rabi example. Local rainfall and irrigation can change the planting schedule.
Major crops are rice, wheat, millets, pulses, sugarcane, cotton, jute, tea and coffee.
Rice grows in the wet plains and deltas, wheat in the Ganga plains, tea in Assam and the Nilgiris and cotton in black soil regions.
Soils include alluvial, black, red, laterite and desert soils.
Irrigation by canals, tanks and wells supports farming.
The Green Revolution brought high-yielding seeds, and issues like soil erosion need soil conservation.
Soil includes mineral particles, organic matter, air and water. Its texture and nutrients affect which plants can grow well.

board.text: Soil is more than loose rock

text.en: The Northern Plains and some deltas have extensive river deposits. The texture may vary from coarse sand to fine clay.
Many black soils contain a high proportion of clay and can hold water for longer. Cotton is a familiar association, though it can grow in other suitable soils.
Red soils occur in parts of the plateau and elsewhere. Their usefulness for crops also depends on water, organic matter and how land is managed.

board.text: Red soil colour often comes from iron compounds

text.en: In some hot, wet areas rainwater carries dissolved materials downward. This process, called leaching, shapes laterite soils.

board.text: Heavy rainfall can affect laterite soils

text.en: Water running down bare slopes and strong wind over exposed soil can move its upper layers. Vegetation cover and careful slope management can help limit loss.
An irrigation system supplies water when rain is not enough or arrives at the wrong time. Canals, tanks and wells provide different sources.
A canal moves water from a source to farmland. A tank collects and stores water so that some is available after rain has stopped.

board.text: Canals carry water and tanks store it

text.en: A well draws from water held below the surface. If more is withdrawn than is replenished over time, the water level can fall.
Instead of wetting the whole surface, drip systems deliver small amounts near the plants. They can reduce some losses when well maintained.

board.text: Drip irrigation delivers water close to roots

text.en: Many farmers sow crops such as rice or maize near the onset of the southwest monsoon. Expected rainfall and regional conditions affect their timing.
Wheat, mustard and gram are familiar rabi crops. They often use soil moisture left after the monsoon or receive irrigation.

board.text: Rabi crops grow in cooler months

text.en: Crops such as watermelon and cucumber can grow between the main rabi harvest and kharif sowing where water is available.

board.text: Zaid is a short summer season

text.en: Subsistence farming mainly supports the household. Commercial farming produces mainly for sale. A farm can serve both purposes.
Rice commonly needs warm conditions and a reliable water supply. Wheat grows well in a cooler growing season and normally ripens in warmer, drier weather.

board.text: Rice and wheat suit different conditions

text.en: Some millets can grow under drier conditions than rice. Pulses contribute protein to diets and can be included in rotations.
Tea and coffee are beverage crops. Cotton and jute supply fibres. The growing conditions and markets for each crop differ.

board.text: Plantation and fibre crops have different uses

text.en: Animals can supply milk, eggs, manure and additional income. Their care depends on reliable feed, water and services.
Marine fisheries operate at sea. Inland fisheries use waters such as rivers, tanks or ponds. Both can contribute food and livelihoods.
Higher-yielding crop varieties were part of changes involving irrigation, fertiliser and other inputs. Their effects were uneven across places and crops.

board.text: The Green Revolution involved several inputs

text.en: Overdrawing groundwater or allowing erosion can damage future production. Different farms need responses suited to their land and water supplies.

board.text: Growing more also needs sound resource use

text.en: Compare crop requirements, seasonal conditions and available resources. No one soil, season or water source explains every farming choice.

problem.en: Why is cotton grown in black soil?

text.en: Black soil holds moisture.
It is fertile.
Cotton needs such soil.

problem.en: Why might farmers in two districts sow the same crop at different times?

text.en: The onset of rain and access to irrigation can differ.

why.en: Crop calendars depend on local conditions.

text.en: Broad season names help compare patterns but do not fix an exact sowing day.

why.en: Farmers match decisions to the local environment.

problem.en: A village tank holds water for weeks after a storm. What agricultural role can it play?

text.en: The tank stores part of the rainwater.

why.en: Storage makes some water available after the rain ends.

text.en: Stored water can supplement rainfall when fields need irrigation.

why.en: This differs from drawing groundwater through a well.

problem.en: Why might a farmer protect a slope with vegetation?

text.en: Roots help hold soil and surface cover slows runoff.

why.en: Bare ground is more exposed to rain impact and running water.

text.en: Less topsoil may be carried away.

why.en: Retaining topsoil helps protect future production.

prompt.en: A friend says Wheat is a Kharif crop. How will you reply?

points.en: Kharif sowing often follows the onset of the southwest monsoon.
Rabi crops are usually sown after the monsoon and harvested in spring.
